description: Multi-state selection AND per-row removal in the Send Quotation dialog (user tasks 1 & 2). These are combined because both thread through the same pricing-table state (filtered plans, price overrides, and the email HTML builder) in src/components/send-quotation-dialog.tsx. Task 1: after choosing Service Type, allow selecting MULTIPLE states at once so one quotation covers several states; the pricing table and generated email must show plans across all selected states together. Keep the existing single-state + city flow working. Task 2 (FRONTEND ONLY, no backend delete): let the rep drop individual city/location rows from THIS quotation via a cross (x) control at the END of each pricing row (after the Total column). Removing a row only excludes it from the current table + outgoing email HTML; underlying plans/sheet are untouched.
steps: Read src/components/send-quotation-dialog.tsx fully first (buildQuotationHtml through the send flow and the JSX form) so state threads correctly through preview + send + email HTML.

MULTI-STATE state model: replace the single `selectedState: string` with support for multiple states. Recommended: keep `selectedState` for the primary/single path but add `selectedStates: string[]` (or convert to an array and derive a single-state label when length===1). Choose the cleanest approach that does not break the current single-state + city flow. When multiple states are selected, the city sub-select should be hidden/disabled (city filtering only makes sense for a single state) - document this behavior.

MULTI-STATE UI: build a multi-select control using the EXISTING primitives already in src/components/ui (Popover + Command + Checkbox, or Popover + Checkbox list). Do NOT invent a new dependency. Follow the shadcn multi-select pattern: a Popover trigger button showing 'N states selected' / the single state name, containing a scrollable checkbox list of `states` (the existing useMemo-derived unique states). Include a way to pick a single state (existing behavior) and multiple. The user described it as: after Service Type, the State control offers a 'multiple states' capability where the rep ticks several states.

MULTI-STATE filtering: update the `filteredPlans` useMemo so that when multiple states are selected it filters `p.state` against ALL selected states (case-insensitive), instead of the single `selectedState`. When exactly one state is selected, preserve the existing single-state + optional city behavior. Update `locationLabel` so the email/subject reflect all chosen states (e.g. join state names with commas, or 'Multiple States' with a count) - pick a clean readable label and note the choice in findings.

ROW REMOVAL state: add a `removedRowKeys` (Set<string>) or `removedIndexes` in component state. Prefer a STABLE key per plan (e.g. `${p.code}|${p.city}|${p.area}` or index-into-filtered) so removals survive re-render; note that priceOverrides is currently keyed by array index, so keep the keying scheme consistent and re-check that removing rows does not misalign priceOverrides with the wrong plan. The safest approach: compute a `displayPlans` array = filteredPlans minus removed, and key BOTH price overrides and removal by a stable plan identity rather than raw filtered index. Refactor priceOverrides keying if needed to stay correct after removals.

ROW REMOVAL UI: in the React editor pricing table (the `filteredPlans.slice(0,10).map` block), add a trailing table cell AFTER the Total column with a small ghost/icon button (X icon from lucide-react, already used elsewhere) that removes that row from the current quotation. Add a header cell for it (can be empty). Also handle the 'slice(0,10)' truncation: removal must work against the real list, and the '+ N more plans' note must reflect the post-removal count. Provide a lightweight reset/undo affordance (nice-to-have): e.g. a 'Restore all rows' link shown when any rows are removed.

EMAIL + SEND threading: ensure the plans passed into buildQuotationHtml (the `emailHtml` useMemo and the `plansWithOverrides` mapping) use the SAME post-removal, multi-state `displayPlans` set, so the outgoing email and preview exactly match the editor table. Confirm the price-override mapping still lines up with the correct plan after removals/multi-state. Update the emailHtml useMemo dependency array accordingly.

Reset behavior: when the dialog re-opens (the existing `useEffect` on `open`) and when service type changes / states change, reset removedRows and priceOverrides consistently (the code already resets priceOverrides on state change - extend to the new state).

Keep the guard logic working: Preview/Send buttons are disabled when there are no plans; update the disabled conditions to consider the post-removal displayPlans length and the multi-state selection (at least one state selected).
acceptance_criteria: A rep can select multiple states at once from the State control after choosing a Service Type, using existing ui primitives (no new dependency).
With multiple states selected, the editor pricing table and the generated email HTML include plans from ALL selected states.
The existing single-state selection (and its optional city sub-select) continues to work unchanged.
Each pricing row in the editor has an X control after the Total column that removes that row from the current quotation only.
Removing rows updates the editor table, the '+ N more' note, the preview, and the outgoing email HTML consistently; price overrides remain aligned to the correct plans.
No backend/sheet delete occurs - removal is purely in-memory for the current send (getSheetPlans / supabase are not called to delete anything).
locationLabel / subject reflect the selected state(s).
verification: Code inspection: trace selectedStates -> filteredPlans -> displayPlans -> plansWithOverrides -> buildQuotationHtml and confirm the same set flows into both the editor table and emailHtml.
Confirm no supabase delete/mutation call was added for row removal.
Confirm multi-select uses only existing src/components/ui primitives.

findings:
Implemented in src/components/send-quotation-dialog.tsx.

MULTI-STATE UX (task 1): Replaced the single-value shadcn Select for state with a shadcn-style multi-select built from EXISTING primitives only (Popover + Command + Checkbox + Button trigger with ChevronsUpDown icon). State is now `selectedStates: string[]`. A derived `isSingleState = selectedStates.length === 1` and `selectedState = isSingleState ? selectedStates[0] : ""` preserve the classic single-state + optional-city path with zero behavior change. The trigger button shows 'Select state(s)' / the single state name / 'N states selected'. Each Command row is a Checkbox + state name; onSelect toggles membership. filteredPlans now matches p.state (case-insensitive) against the Set of ALL selected states. No new dependency added.

CITY behavior: The city sub-select only renders when exactly one state is selected (`isSingleState && cities.length > 0`). When 2+ states are selected the city select is hidden and selectedCity is cleared, and an inline note explains 'plans from all of them are combined; city filtering is disabled'. City filtering only applies on the single-state path.

locationLabel format (used in email body + subject): 0 states -> 'India'; single state + city -> 'City, State'; single state -> 'State'; 2-3 states -> comma-joined names (e.g. 'Rajasthan, Karnataka'); 4+ states -> 'N States'. This threads unchanged into buildQuotationHtml's `location` and into the subject line.

ROW REMOVAL (task 2, FRONTEND ONLY): Added `removedRowKeys: Set<string>`. Each pricing row gets an X (lucide) ghost icon button in a NEW trailing table cell after the Total column (with an empty header cell), which adds that row's stable key to removedRowKeys. No supabase/getSheetPlans delete or mutation is performed - removal is purely in-memory for the current send. A 'Restore all rows' link appears next to the Pricing label whenever any rows are removed, and the label shows a ' · N removed' counter.

STABLE KEYING (correctness): priceOverrides was previously keyed by the raw filteredPlans array index, which misaligns when rows are removed or states combine duplicates. Introduced planKey(p, idx) = `${code}|${state}|${city}|${area}|${idx}` (idx disambiguates duplicate sheet rows). Built `keyedFilteredPlans = filteredPlans.map((p,i) => ({key: planKey(p,i), plan: p}))` and `displayPlans = keyedFilteredPlans.filter(({key}) => !removedRowKeys.has(key))`. priceOverrides is now Record<string, number> keyed by planKey. Because the key embeds the index into the STABLE filteredPlans list (which does not shrink on removal - only displayPlans shrinks), overrides and removals never drift onto the wrong plan.

EMAIL/SEND threading: emailHtml now maps `displayPlans` (post-removal, multi-state) applying priceOverrides by key, so the outgoing email and preview exactly match the editor table. emailHtml dependency array updated to [.., displayPlans, priceOverrides, ..]. handleSend and both Preview/Send disabled guards now use displayPlans.length and selectedStates.length (>=1) instead of filteredPlans.length / !selectedState. The '+ N more plans' truncation note and the editor slice(0,10) now operate on displayPlans so the count reflects post-removal totals; the email still includes ALL displayPlans (buildQuotationHtml maps the full list).

RESETS: The open useEffect resets selectedStates (from defaultState), selectedCity, serviceType, priceOverrides, removedRowKeys, and closes the state popover. toggleState() (any state add/remove) resets selectedCity, priceOverrides, and removedRowKeys, mirroring the previous reset-on-state-change.

STYLE: em dash avoided in the inline note (used a colon). Matched existing useState/useMemo + shadcn usage; PopoverContent width uses w-[var(--radix-popover-trigger-width)] to match the codebase's existing var(...) convention in ui/select.tsx.

VERIFICATION LIMITATION: Sandbox is INTEGRATIONS_ONLY - bun install fails (npm 403), so bun run build / lint / typecheck / dev server could NOT be run. Verified by careful code inspection and consistency with existing patterns only. CI must run typecheck/lint/build to fully validate. Traced selectedStates -> filteredPlans -> keyedFilteredPlans -> displayPlans -> plansWithOverrides -> buildQuotationHtml; confirmed the same post-removal multi-state set flows into both the editor table and emailHtml, and confirmed no supabase delete/mutation was added for row removal.

V1 REVIEW FOLLOW-UP (non-blocking, review APPROVED): The v1 review noted that the Service Type Select's onValueChange (setServiceType) reset neither priceOverrides nor removedRowKeys, unlike toggleState(). With identity-based planKeys this only caused dormant overrides/removals to silently reactivate if a rep flipped service type away and back with the same states selected. Fixed by extending the service-type onValueChange handler to also call setPriceOverrides({}) and setRemovedRowKeys(new Set()), matching toggleState() and the open-effect reset. Minimal change, no other behavior touched. Verified by inspection only (INTEGRATIONS_ONLY sandbox; build/lint/typecheck still cannot run).
